_what_this_is: The complete input contract for build_dashboard.py. It is valid JSON so you can load it, but it is documentation: keys beginning with an underscore are annotations, not data. A real tree has no underscore keys.
_how_to_use_it: build_dashboard.py reads FOUR things and nothing else. It never touches a raw recording.
If your processing code can emit these four, you get the dashboard - whatever produced the numbers.
generate_template_data.py, beside this file, writes a complete, valid example of all four. Run it, diff your own exporter against what it produces, and you are done.
Every field below is annotated with whether the dashboard actually READS it. Fields marked read=false are written by pipeline.py and kept for provenance; the dashboard ignores them.

_the_four_inputs.outputs/cognitive_load.json: One entry per TASK recording: identity, status, QC, and which baseline it pairs with.
_the_four_inputs.outputs/baselines.json: One entry per BASELINE recording, each carrying its segments.
_the_four_inputs.outputs/variants/index.json: The sweep manifest: every axis, every threshold, and one entry per swept unit.
_the_four_inputs.outputs/variants/*_e<NN.N>.npz: The numbers. Two files per window length - tasks and baselines.

_units_and_keys.recording key: '<participant>/<recording>', e.g. 't01/task_agent_personal'. Used as the key in cognitive_load.json and baselines.json.
_units_and_keys.archive key: The same string for a task. For a baseline it is segment-qualified: '<participant>/<recording>::<segment>'. Each baseline segment is its own swept unit because each is cropped and calibrated on its own samples.
_units_and_keys.array_prefix: The archive key with '/' replaced by '~'. This is what every array name inside the .npz files starts with.
_units_and_keys.amplitudes: microvolts, robust standard deviation (MAD/0.6745), unless a field name says otherwise
_units_and_keys.times: seconds from the start of the segment
_units_and_keys.arm and framing: read from the recording NAME by build_dashboard.condition_label(): '_agent_' / '_ai_' / '_none_' and 'personal' / 'speedscore'. Rename your recordings to match, or edit that function.

partial_run._note: true makes build_dashboard.py REFUSE. A filtered pipeline run must not produce a published dashboard.

run_meta._other_fields: generated_utc, argv, n_discovered, n_processed, excluded_participants, excluded_recordings, parameters - kept for provenance, not read here.

recording._note: arm and framing are parsed out of this string

status._note: anything other than 'ok' sends the recording to the excluded table instead of the charts

exclusion_reason._note: printed verbatim in the excluded table. A status token alone tells the reader nothing.

qc_segment._read: segment_duration_s, segment_elapsed_s, n_internal_gaps, max_internal_gap_s, repair, notes

segment_elapsed_s._note: wall-clock span. Differs from duration when samples were excised.

repair._note: a sentence describing any splice, shown on the panel

per_channel._read: robust_sd_uv, for the five channels in peak_channels
per_channel._note: Amplitude AS RECORDED: after filtering, before interpolation, in the hardware reference. This is what the quality badge judges against the derived band. Deliberately not the amplitude of whatever is currently plotted.

bad_channels_detected._note: THE PAIRED LIST. Decided once per task/baseline pair, from the task concatenated with the rest segment of its baseline, and interpolated identically in both. Detecting per recording puts a spline on one side of a ratio and raw artifact on the other - it disagreed in 14 of 22 pairs on the real dataset.

example._note: the reference notebook's own per-recording detection, kept so that step is reproducible

qc_ocular._read: a whitelist of keys per mode, shown on the panel
qc_ocular._note: One entry per ocular mode. The baseline's own qc_ocular is read too and shown on the TASK panel - a correction that injects artifact into the baseline corrupts the denominator of every value there.

holm._note: per-window index. Written by pipeline.py; the dashboard reads the .npz arrays instead.

qc_gate._note: vestigial. The amplitude gate was removed in 2026-09; nothing is withheld.

baseline._note: null when status is not ok

interpolated._note: MUST equal the paired task's bad_channels_detected. Both sides of every ratio are interpolated on one list.

segments._note: One entry per baseline segment. The keys must match index.json's baseline_segment_order.

amplitude._note: Per segment, not per block. The eyes-closed slice can be a very different electrode picture from the rest phase - 8 of 22 baselines differed on the real dataset.

implausible_channels._note: channels outside the derived amplitude band

qc_segment._read: notes, used to explain an unusable baseline

qc_ocular._note: same whitelist as the task's; shown on the paired task's panel

outputs/variants/index.json._note: The manifest. build_dashboard.py validates this hard and refuses rather than building something wrong - see _refusals at the end of this file.

bad_channel_detection._note: Anything else is a REFUSAL. It is the record that one bad-channel list was decided per task/baseline pair.

value_keys._note: COLUMN ORDER of every ::v:: array. Load-bearing.

peak_channels._note: COLUMN ORDER of every ::p:: and ::s:: array. Load-bearing.

ocular_modes._note: Checked for ORDERED equality against the page's own list. Position matters: the first entry is taken as the uncorrected branch.

interpolation_modes._note: Also checked for ordered equality. 'on'/'manual' are the source; '_keepfrontal' is the same source with the frontal pair held back.

manual_interpolation._note: keyed '<participant>|<arm>'; shown on the page as the hand-picked list

robust_slide_choices_s._note: the Calibration window toggle. One stored sigma matrix per entry, which is why it is a toggle and not a slider.

amplitude_bound._note: The band outside which a channel is UNUSUAL FOR THIS RUN. available=false is a REFUSAL. Fit it on your own run's amplitudes - a fixed range invented in advance is what this replaced. Read it as relative, never as a physiological standard.

_value.method: pooled across channels; log10; spread from (median - p25)/0.6745 so the upper tail cannot set its own threshold; +/- k sigma
_value.basis: this run's own channel amplitudes (relative, not absolute)

recordings._note: One entry per SWEPT UNIT: every task, and every baseline SEGMENT separately.

segment._note: null for a task; the segment name for a baseline

bad_channels._note: the detected list, for the badge

interpolation_lists._note: Which channels each mode replaces. An entry for EVERY mode is required - the page describes what each one did from this map. Missing entries are a refusal.

interpolation_tokens._note: mode -> stored-array token. The archive is keyed by WHICH CHANNELS were interpolated, not by mode name, so modes reaching the same list share one array. Token is '+'.join(channels in montage order), or '-' for none. Missing is a refusal. A task and its baseline segments MUST resolve to the same tokens.

references_failed._note: a reference that could not be applied; its variants are absent and the page says so

sigma._note: whole-recording robust SD per channel, per ocular mode

amplitude_displayed._note: Amplitude of what is actually PLOTTED, keyed '<token>|<ocular>|<reference>'. One entry per distinct token x ocular x reference. The page shows this beside the as-recorded figure, because re-referencing smears one broken electrode across all ten.

motion_unavailable_reason._note: a sentence, shown on the panel. A flat sensor is NO sensor, not a perfectly still head.

excluded_windows._note: Per epoch length, window indices whose samples are not contiguous in real time. Dropped under EVERY artifact mode including None - that mode means 'do not judge the EEG', not 'plot everything'. The field must be present; absent is a refusal.

band_bins._note: Bins per band per '<epoch>|<estimator>'. A pure function of the sampling rate, so EVERY recording must report an identical table - differing tables mean something resampled, and the build refuses.

times_s._note: TASKS ONLY (null for a baseline). RECORDED window start times - never spread duration evenly over window indices, which put one real window four minutes wrong.

window_index._note: BASELINES ONLY (null for a task). A baseline ships no per-window times, so the page assumes a contiguous grid.

default_check._note: per-column deviations of the default cell from MNE's own estimator. NON-EMPTY IS A REFUSAL.

default_verified._note: false, or absent, IS A REFUSAL. An empty default_check with nothing compared is not a pass.

_filenames: tasks_e04.0.npz     -> every TASK at the 4 s window length
baselines_e04.0.npz -> every BASELINE SEGMENT at 4 s
one pair per entry in epochs_s; the name format is f"{'tasks'|'baselines'}_e{epoch:04.1f}.npz"
outputs/variants/*_e<NN.N>.npz._dtype: float32. build_dashboard.py re-casts to little-endian '<f4' and base64s it straight into the page, so nothing is rounded on the way to the browser.

<prefix>::v::<token>|<ocular>|<reference.count: distinct tokens x 3 ocular x 3 references x 4 estimators, per unit per epoch

<prefix>::p::<ocular>.meaning: per-window peak amplitude in microvolts, what the Robust and Absolute cap sliders threshold
<prefix>::p::<ocular>._note: Measured on the PRE-INTERPOLATION signal in the hardware reference, whatever is displayed. A spline is smooth by construction and passes an amplitude threshold far more readily than a real electrode.

<prefix>::s::<ocular>|<calibration lengt.meaning: per-window robust sigma from the N seconds CENTRED on each window, for the Windowed Robust mode
<prefix>::s::<ocular>|<calibration lengt._note: The one browser-side threshold that cannot be derived from what the page already has, which is why it is stored per offered length. Length is formatted %g: '10', '20', '30'.

<prefix>::m::imu.columns: motion_columns, in order: accel_jerk, gyro, n_aux_samples
<prefix>::m::imu._note: ONE matrix per unit per epoch - no ocular, reference or estimator dimension, because the IMU is a property of the recording rather than of a processing choice. OMIT the array entirely when there is no usable sensor; the page then counts those windows as unassessed rather than as clean.

outputs/variants/*_e<NN.N>.npz._missing_arrays: An array the sweep did not produce is not an error. build_dashboard.py records it in a `missing` list and the page reports 'the pipeline never built this variant' rather than 'this recording has no windows here'. Those are different facts and readers act on them differently.

_refusals: run_meta.partial_run is true -> a filtered run must not produce a published dashboard
any recording is missing default_verified, or has it false
any recording has a non-empty default_check
ocular_modes differs from ['none','eog_regression','ica'] in value OR order
interpolation_modes differs from ['off','on','on_keepfrontal','manual','manual_keepfrontal'] in value OR order
any recording's interpolation_lists lacks an entry for some mode
two recordings report different band_bins tables
a baseline's three segments were swept with different interpolation tokens
a task and its baseline resolve interpolation modes to different stored arrays

_known_limitation.dataset_specific_prose: About 15 passages in build_dashboard.py's page template state findings from the Sarma Lab's own dataset as fact - 'positive on all 21 recordings with a working sensor', 'one 20-minute task recording', and similar. Those sentences will appear verbatim on a dashboard built from YOUR data, where they are not true. Grep build_dashboard.py for 'on this dataset', '21 recordings' and '20-minute' before publishing a build of your own.
